citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

Choose an embedded smooth submanifold $S\subset X$ of codimension $k$, a smooth positive density $\mu_S$, and an open neighborhood $U\subset X$ of a point $s\in S$. Embedded means that near each point of $S$, a smooth chart on $X$ identifies $S$ with $\mathbb R^{n-k}\times\{0\}$. A **gauge condition** on $U$ is a smooth map $\chi:U\to\mathbb R^k$ such that $U\cap S=\chi^{-1}(0)$ and, for every $s'\in U\cap S$, $d\chi_{s'}$ is surjective with kernel $T_{s'}S$. For every $x\in U$, the **infinitesimal orbit map** is $R_x:=d(\alpha_x)_e:\mathfrak k\to T_xX$, where $\alpha_x(g)=x\cdot g$; call its kernel the infinitesimal stabilizer at $x$. The **Faddeev–Popov operator** at $x$ is the ordinary linear map $M_x:=d\chi_x\circ R_x:\mathfrak k\to\mathbb R^k$. At a slice point $s'\in U\cap S$, call the condition **transverse** when $M_{s'}$ is an isomorphism. Choose a positive density $\nu$ on $\mathfrak k$ equal to $(\mu_K)_e$, and the standard positive density $\lambda$ on $\mathbb R^k$. For every $x\in U$, the finite-dimensional Faddeev–Popov Jacobian $\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}(x)$ is the nonnegative density ratio defined by $M_x^*\lambda=\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}(x)\nu$; in chosen bases it is $|\det M_x|$, and it is zero when $M_x$ is singular.

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be
$C^1$, and let $a\in U$.  If $Df(a)$ is invertible, then there are open sets
$V,W\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $a\in V\subseteq U$ and $f(a)\in W$ such that
$f|_V:V\to W$ is bijective.  Its inverse $g:W\to V$ is $C^1$, and

$$Dg(y)=Df(g(y))^{-1}\qquad(y\in W).$$

Thus $f$ is a local diffeomorphism at $a$.

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, and let $g:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be injective and $C^1$, with $Dg(x)$ invertible on $U$. Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be compactly supported Riemann integrable and suppose $\operatorname{supp}f\subseteq g(U)$. Define
$$h(x)=\begin{cases}f(g(x))|\det Dg(x)|,&x\in U,\\0,&x\notin U.\end{cases}$$
Then $h$ is compactly supported Riemann integrable and
$$\int_{\mathbb R^n}f(y)\,dy=\int_{\mathbb R^n}h(x)\,dx.$$

citations.quote: A **finite-dimensional regulated gauge-slice datum** consists of integers $1\le k\le n$; a finite-dimensional Lie group $K$ of dimension $k$, with Lie algebra $\mathfrak k:=T_eK$ and bracket transported from left-invariant vector fields; a chosen smooth positive left-invariant density $\mu_K$, meaning $(L_h^K)^*\mu_K=\mu_K$ for $L_h^K(g)=hg$; a finite-dimensional smooth manifold $X$ of dimension $n$ with a chosen smooth positive density $\mu_X$; and a smooth right action $\alpha:X\times K\to X$, written $x\cdot g$, with $x\cdot e=x$ and $(x\cdot g)\cdot h=x\cdot(gh)$. A smooth positive density on an $m$-manifold has coordinate form $\rho(x)|dx^1\cdots dx^m|$ with smooth $\rho>0$, and transforms by the absolute coordinate Jacobian. The group $K$ and its action on $X$ are separate regulator data. They are not identified with the full gauge group or the full space of connections unless a particular finite model explicitly constructs such an action and verifies that it preserves $X$.

Choose an embedded smooth submanifold $S\subset X$ of codimension $k$, a smooth positive density $\mu_S$, and an open neighborhood $U\subset X$ of a point $s\in S$. Embedded means that near each point of $S$, a smooth chart on $X$ identifies $S$ with $\mathbb R^{n-k}\times\{0\}$. A **gauge condition** on $U$ is a smooth map $\chi:U\to\mathbb R^k$ such that $U\cap S=\chi^{-1}(0)$ and, for every $s'\in U\cap S$, $d\chi_{s'}$ is surjective with kernel $T_{s'}S$. For every $x\in U$, the **infinitesimal orbit map** is $R_x:=d(\alpha_x)_e:\mathfrak k\to T_xX$, where $\alpha_x(g)=x\cdot g$; call its kernel the infinitesimal stabilizer at $x$. The **Faddeev–Popov operator** at $x$ is the ordinary linear map $M_x:=d\chi_x\circ R_x:\mathfrak k\to\mathbb R^k$. At a slice point $s'\in U\cap S$, call the condition **transverse** when $M_{s'}$ is an isomorphism. Choose a positive density $\nu$ on $\mathfrak k$ equal to $(\mu_K)_e$, and the standard positive density $\lambda$ on $\mathbb R^k$. For every $x\in U$, the finite-dimensional Faddeev–Popov Jacobian $\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}(x)$ is the nonnegative density ratio defined by $M_x^*\lambda=\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}(x)\nu$; in chosen bases it is $|\det M_x|$, and it is zero when $M_x$ is singular.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and let $(X,K,\alpha,S,\chi,\mu_X,\mu_K,\mu_S)$ be finite-dimensional regulated gauge-slice data as defined above, with $\dim X=n$, $\dim K=k$, $1\le k\le n$, and $s_0\in S\cap U$. Thus $K$ acts smoothly on the right, $S$ is an embedded codimension-$k$ submanifold, $\chi:U\to\mathbb R^k$ is a smooth defining submersion with $\ker d\chi_s=T_sS$, and the Faddeev–Popov operator is $M_s=d\chi_s\circ R_s$. Suppose $M_{s_0}$ is an isomorphism. For $\Psi(g,s)=s\cdot g$, there are neighborhoods $V$ of the identity in $K$, $W$ of $s_0$ in $S$, and $O$ of $s_0$ in $X$ such that $\Psi:V\times W\to O$ is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism. Consequently, each orbit has exactly one representative in $W$ among the representatives reached using $V$.

Fix group coordinates $\xi$ near the identity, slice coordinates $z$ near $s_0$, and adapted target coordinates $(y,z)=(\chi,z)$ near $s_0$. Write the densities there as $\mu_K=\rho_K(\xi)|d\xi|$, $\mu_S=\rho_S(z)|dz|$, and $\mu_X=\rho_X(y,z)|dy\,dz|$. The positive Jacobian $J_\Psi$ defined by $\Psi^*\mu_X=J_\Psi(\mu_K\otimes\mu_S)$ satisfies

$$
J_\Psi(e,s_0)=\frac{\rho_X(0,z_0)}{\rho_S(z_0)}\,\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}(s_0),
$$

where $\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}$ uses the density $(\mu_K)_e$ and the standard density on $\mathbb R^k$. Thus, when the target and slice densities are normalized so that $\rho_X(0,z_0)=\rho_S(z_0)$, the ordinary finite-dimensional orbit-to-slice Jacobian is exactly $\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}(s_0)$. For every compactly supported Riemann-integrable function $f:O\to\mathbb R$, the local change-of-variables identity is
$$
\int_O f\,d\mu_X=\int_{V\times W}(f\circ\Psi)J_\Psi\,d\mu_K\,d\mu_S.
$$

For the exact multiplicity statement, fix $x\in X$ and a relatively compact open set $\Gamma\subset K$ such that $x\cdot\overline{\Gamma}\subset U$. Let $F_x(g)=\chi(x\cdot g)$. Let $r\ge 0$ be finite, and suppose $F_x$ has exactly $r$ zeros $g_1,\ldots,g_r$ in the support of a smooth function $\varphi$ compactly supported in $\Gamma$, each $M_{x\cdot g_i}$ is invertible, and the slice points $s_i=x\cdot g_i$ are distinct. Choose a nonnegative $\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^k)$, supported in a ball $B_C(0)$ of finite radius $C>0$, with integral $1$, and set $\eta_\epsilon(y)=\epsilon^{-k}\eta(y/\epsilon)$. Then

$$
\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\int_\Gamma \varphi(g)\,\eta_\epsilon(F_x(g))\,\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}(x\cdot g)\,d\mu_K(g)=\sum_{i=1}^r\varphi(g_i).
$$

In particular, if $\varphi=1$ near the zeros, this finite-regulator expression counts the $r$ distinct transverse intersections exactly. The theorem asserts only a local chart and this finite-dimensional multiplicity formula; it gives no global gauge section, functional determinant, or continuum path-integral measure.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every open cover of a smooth manifold admits a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact, connected, oriented, boundaryless smooth manifold of dimension $d\in\{3,4\}$ with a smooth Riemannian metric, let $N\ge2$, and fix a smooth right principal $SU(N)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$, a smooth connection $A_0$, and a point $p_m\in P$ over $x_m\in M$. Use the standard unitary representation of $SU(N)$ on $\mathbb C^N$ and the invariant positive inner product $\langle X,Y\rangle=-\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ on $\mathfrak{su}(N)$. Define the adjoint vector bundle $\operatorname{ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}\mathfrak{su}(N)$ and the adjoint group bundle $\operatorname{Ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}SU(N)$ with associated-bundle relation $[pg,z]=[p,\operatorname{Ad}_g z]$.

Choose one finite smooth bundle atlas with relatively compact coordinate domains and a subordinate partition of unity. For each integer $k>d/2+1$, let $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$ be the Sobolev completions of smooth sections in the resulting finite-atlas norms. Define the affine configuration space $\mathcal A_k:=A_0+H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and the set $\mathcal G_{k+1}:=H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ of Sobolev gauge sections. The next lemma proves that the pointwise product and inverse close on this set and make it a Hilbert Lie group. Its based subset is $\mathcal G_{k+1,m}:=\{u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}:u(p_m)=e\}$. Let $Z_N=\{zI_N:z^N=1\}$ be the center of $SU(N)$, viewed as constant gauge sections. Indeed, if $Z=(z_{ij})$ is central and $D=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,\ldots,t_N)\in SU(N)$, then $(t_j-t_i)z_{ij}=0$. For each $i\ne j$ one can choose such a diagonal matrix with $t_i\ne t_j$, so $Z$ is diagonal. Commuting with the determinant-one unitary rotation whose block on the $(i,j)$ coordinates is $\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&\sin t\\-\sin t&\cos t\end{pmatrix}$ for $t\notin\pi\mathbb Z$ forces the $i$th and $j$th diagonal entries equal. Hence $Z=zI_N$; determinant one gives $z^N=1$, and conversely every such scalar is central. Write $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$ for the set of $Z_N$-cosets with quotient topology; the next lemma also verifies that the induced pointwise operation makes it a Hilbert Lie group.

Let $\mathcal A_\infty:=A_0+\Omega^1(M,\operatorname{ad}P)$ and let $\mathcal G_\infty$ be the smooth gauge group, with the $C^\infty$ section topology generated by all finite-atlas derivative seminorms. Define $\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty:=\mathcal G_\infty/Z_N$. In a local section of $P$, write a connection as a matrix-valued one-form $A$ and a gauge section as a map $u$ into $SU(N)$; the right gauge action is $A^u:=u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$, equivalently pullback by the gauge automorphism associated with $u$. The calculus lemma proves that this formula defines a smooth action on the Sobolev spaces above. For an adjoint section $\xi$, set $d_A\xi:=d\xi+[A,\xi]$ using the degree-one Lie-algebra-valued-form bracket. In local coordinates and an orthonormal adjoint frame, define the formal adjoint on an adjoint-valued one-form $a$ by $(d_A^*a)=-g^{ij}(\nabla_i^{\mathrm{LC}}a_j+[A_i,a_j])$, where $\nabla^{\mathrm{LC}}$ differentiates the covector index. This is the $L^2$ adjoint for the Riemannian volume and stated fiber metric; its local coefficient formula defines a distribution at Sobolev regularity.

For $A\in\mathcal A_k$, parallel transport of its $C^1$ connection form around piecewise smooth loops based at $p_m$ defines a subgroup $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)\subseteq SU(N)$. Call $A$ irreducible when this subgroup leaves no nonzero proper complex subspace of $\mathbb C^N$ invariant; changing the chosen frame conjugates the subgroup and leaves this condition unchanged. Write $\mathcal A_k^*$ and $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ for the irreducible loci. Once the calculus lemma verifies the group action, define orbit equivalence by $A\sim B$ exactly when $B=A^u$ for some gauge section $u$; all resulting quotients carry the quotient topology, whose open sets are those with open inverse image under the orbit projection.

Assume the configuration data and integer $k>d/2+1$ from the first definition. The irreducible locus $\mathcal A_k^*$ is open, and the orbit projection

$$\pi_k:\mathcal A_k^*\longrightarrow \mathcal A_k^*/\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$$

is a locally trivial smooth principal Banach Lie group bundle. For every $A\in\mathcal A_k^*$ there is an $\varepsilon>0$ such that the Coulomb slice

$$S_{A,\varepsilon}:=\{A+a:a\in\ker d_A^*,\ \|a\|_{H^k}<\varepsilon\}$$

lies in $\mathcal A_k^*$, meets each orbit in its saturation exactly once, and has open saturation. The map $S_{A,\varepsilon}\to\pi_k(S_{A,\varepsilon})$ is a smooth chart of the quotient, whose quotient topology is Hausdorff.

For the $C^\infty$ connection and gauge spaces with the section topologies specified in the first definition, the irreducible projection

$$\pi_\infty:\mathcal A_\infty^*\longrightarrow\mathcal A_\infty^*/\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty$$

is a locally trivial topological principal $\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty$-bundle with the actual $C^\infty$ quotient topology. No inverse-limit assertion alone is used to obtain this smooth-space conclusion.

Assume ZF together with the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be $S^3$ or $S^4$, let $N\ge2$, and let $P\to M$ be any smooth principal right $SU(N)$-bundle. Fix a smooth reference connection $A_0$, a basepoint $m\in M$, and a frame of $P_m$. Equip the affine space $\mathcal A_\infty=A_0+\Omega^1(M;\operatorname{ad}P)$ with its $C^\infty$ section topology, and let $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ be the connections whose based holonomy action on $\mathbb C^N$ has no nonzero proper invariant complex subspace. Then $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ is nonempty and path-connected, and for every $A\in\mathcal A_\infty^*$ and every integer $j\ge1$, $\pi_j(\mathcal A_\infty^*,A)=0$. Here $\pi_j(X,x)$ is the based homotopy group of continuous maps $u:(I^j,\partial I^j)\to(X,x)$ modulo homotopies that keep $\partial I^j$ at $x$.

Let $r\in\{3,4\}$, $N\ge2$, and $P\to S^r$ be any smooth principal $SU(N)$ bundle. Write $\mathcal G(P):=\mathcal G_\infty(P)$ for its smooth gauge group with the finite-atlas $C^\infty$ section topology and $\overline{\mathcal G}(P):=\overline{\mathcal G}_\infty(P)=\mathcal G_\infty(P)/Z_N$ for the quotient by constant central gauge sections. Then either $\overline{\mathcal G}(P)$ has more than one path component or at least one of its based homotopy groups $\pi_j(\overline{\mathcal G}(P),e)$, $j\ge1$, is nonzero. More precisely, for $r=3$ it has infinitely many path components, and for $r=4$ its fundamental group is nontrivial.

Let $p:E\to B$ be a nonempty locally trivial principal topological $H$-bundle with right $H$-action, and suppose it has a continuous section. For any $b_0\in B$, the fiber $H$ is a retract of $E$. If $E$ is weakly contractible, then $H$ is path connected and $\pi_j(H,e)=0$ for every $j\ge1$.

The retraction is expressed by the commutative diagram
$$\begin{array}{ccc}H&\xrightarrow{i}&E\\\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle\operatorname{id}_H}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle r}\\H&=&H\end{array}$$
with TikZ source
```tikz
\begin{tikzcd}
H \arrow[r,"i"] \arrow[dr,"\operatorname{id}_H"'] & E \arrow[d,"r"]\\
& H
\end{tikzcd}
```
